﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾, ﴿the King of mankind﴾, ﴿the God of mankind﴾, ﴿from the evil of the sneaking whisperer﴾, ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾, ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾.

Its opening resembles the opening of Surah al-Falaq, except that Surah al-Falaq is a seeking of refuge from the evils of created beings, such as animals and humans, while Surah al-Nas is a seeking of refuge from the evils of hidden created beings, who are the devils (al-shayatin).

The discussion regarding the command to say (this), regarding what is said, and regarding the fact that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) while the intended meaning includes his community, is the same as the discussion of its counterpart in Surah al-Falaq.

"Rabb" is made definite by its being annexed to "al-nas" (mankind), not to other beings that are nurtured, because seeking refuge from the evil that Satan casts into the hearts of people, so that they go astray and lead others astray, means that the evil sought refuge from is directed toward people. It was therefore fitting that the One sought refuge with be brought to mind by the title that He is the Lord of those who cast evil and of those to whom it is cast, so that He may turn these away and repel it from the others, as one says to the master of a slave: "O master of so-and-so, restrain your slave from me."

The attributes of God in relation to people have been arranged in a graduated order. God is their Creator; then they are not outside His judgment when He wills to dispose of their affairs; then He is further clarified by the attribute of His divinity toward them, so that it becomes clear that His lordship over them and His sovereignty over them is not like the lordship of some of them over others and the sovereignty of some of them over others.

In this ordering there is also an indication of the stages of reflection in knowing God, the Exalted. The one who reflects first declares that he has a Lord, on account of what he perceives of his own existence and the blessing of his composition. Then he delves deeper into reflection and perceives that his Lord is the true King, free of need from creation. Then he knows that He is the one deserving of worship, so He is the God of all mankind.

﴿King of mankind﴾ is an apposition (ʿatf al-bayan) to "Lord of mankind," and likewise ﴿God of mankind﴾. The repetition of the word "mankind" rather than suffice with a pronoun is because apposition requires explicitness, so that the explaining noun (in the genitive) is independent in itself, since the apposition stands in the position of a sign for the explained noun (in the accusative).

"Al-nas" is a collective noun for all of humanity or a group of them, and it is not applied, in verification, to anyone other than them.

"Al-waswas" means one who speaks with whispering, and whispering is hidden speech. Ru'ba said, describing a hunter in his hiding place:

"He whispered, calling sincerely upon the Lord of the daybreak."

So "al-waswas" is an active participle. The word "al-waswas" with a fatha on the waw is used figuratively for the thoughts that occur to a person's self, which he imagines, like speech that a person addresses to himself. ʿUrwa ibn Udhayna said:

"And when you find for it whispers of consolation, let the heart intercede with the conscience and then soothe it."

The definite article in "al-waswas" is the definite article of the genus, and the application of "al-waswas" to its literal and figurative meanings includes the devils who cast evil thoughts into people's souls, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But Satan whispered to him﴾ [Taha: 120]. It also includes every person among mankind who speaks hidden speech, namely the people of plots and conspiracies, whose purpose is to inflict harm, whether by assassinating souls, stealing wealth, or enticing [others] into error and turning away from guidance. This is because the custom of these people in discussing with one another is that it be secret, lest those they intend to harm learn of it. These are the ones who lie in wait for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for misfortunes and incite people to harm him.

"Al-khannas" means one who withdraws greatly and frequently. The intended meaning is that it has become a habit for him. "Al-khans" and "al-khunus" mean concealment. Satan is given the epithet "al-khannas" because he attaches himself to a person's intellect and resolve without any awareness on the person's part, so it is as if he has withdrawn into him. And people of deceit, scheming and stealthy approach are "khannasun," because they watch for people's moments of heedlessness and conceal themselves with various kinds of tricks so that people will not perceive them.

The definiteness of "al-khannas" is according to the pattern of the definiteness of the noun it describes. Also, because thoughts of evil occupy their owner's mind, he lowers his head and hesitates and fears their consequences, and the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) restrains him, or the restraint of religion, or shame, or fear of punishment from God or from people restrains him. Then it returns to him until he is at ease with it and becomes accustomed to it, so he resolves to do it and commits it. It is as if Satan appears to him and then disappears, then appears and disappears, until he is able to lower him into delusion with deception.

﴿The sneaking whisperer﴾ is described by ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾ in order to bring the image of whispering closer, so that a person may guard against it when it afflicts him, because of its concealment. This is done by clarifying that the place where whispering is cast is the breasts of people and their inner selves. Thus the breast is used to express the inner psychological sensation, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but greatness, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir: 56]. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Sin is that which stirs in the breast and wavers in the heart." So the ultimate goal of whispering through its whisperings is to spread it into the soul of the deceived one and the one caught in its trap. Thus, the whisperings of the devils are attractions linking souls toward the call of the devils. The Prophet (ﷺ) brought this closer in many reports through various kinds of comparison, among them (that they are like proboscises which Satan extends to the heart of a human being), and he likened it once to blowing, and once to ...[sic: "al-ibsas"] (the coaxing of a beast). And in the hadith: ("Satan runs in the son of Adam as blood runs, and I feared that he would cast [evil] into your hearts.")

The use of the verb "yuwaswisu" (whispers) for this satanic act is figurative, since Satan has no speech in the inner self of a person. As for its application to a person's embellishing of evil deeds for another, it is literal. The attachment of the prepositional phrase in His saying ﴿in the breasts of mankind﴾ to the verb ﴿whispers﴾ is a real attachment with respect to Satan's whispering, while with respect to people's whispering it is a rational figurative attachment, because people's whispering is a cause for its effect to occur in the breasts. So in each of the verb "yuwaswisu" and its complement there is the use of the two expressions both in the literal and the figurative sense.

The "min" in His saying ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾ is explanatory (bayaniyyah). It explains ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾ as being a genus which, considering the intention of its literal and figurative meanings, divides into two categories: one category from the jinn, which is its origin, and another category from mankind, who are only followers and allies of the first category. God combined these two categories in His saying: (﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy: devils among mankind and jinn, who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am: 112]).

The need for this clarification is the hiddenness of what results from the whispering of the human species, because nations are accustomed to their reformers warning them about Satan's whispering, and it may not occur to them that among whisperings there is one worse than the whispering of the devils, namely the whispering of the people of their own kind, which is more dangerous, and they are more deserving of seeking refuge from them, because they are closer to them and it is more hazardous for them, and because they are more capable and more able to cause harm.

It is not correct for "min" to be explanatory of "mankind," since the name "mankind" is not applied to what includes the jinn, and whoever claims that has gone far astray.

"Al-jinnah" is a collective noun for "jinniyy," with the nisba ya' referring to the species of jinn; thus a single "jinniyy" is one of the species of jinn, just as one says "insiyy" for one of mankind.

The repetition of the word "mankind" in these verses, in the first two occurrences, with respect to one meaning, is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, for the purpose of emphasizing God's lordship, His dominion, and His divinity over all of mankind, as in His saying: ﴿They twist their tongues with the Book, that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran: 78].

As for its repetition the third time with His saying ﴿in the breasts of mankind﴾, it is an explicit noun for the sake of the remoteness of the return (to the Hereafter).

As for its repetition the fourth time with His saying ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾, it is because it is an explanation of one of the two categories of "who whispers in the breasts of mankind," and that is not the same referent as the word "mankind" in the previous occurrences.

And God suffices us against the evil of the two groups, and benefits us with the goodness of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn).

The commentary on Surah al-Nas is complete, and with it the commentary on the Mighty Qur'an is complete.

Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur says: I have fulfilled what I intended, and God has realized what I hoped for. I have come with what my effort permitted of explaining the meanings of the Qur'an, the subtleties of its order and the characteristics of its eloquence, drawing from the statements of the imams what the mind could absorb, and striking a spark to illuminate thought and kindle resolve. I have brought what I hope I have been granted success in, to explain truths that are overlooked and subtleties which may have revealed aspects though not fully disclosed their essence, for this is an attainment which the human intellect cannot reach in its entirety, and whoever aspires to that has aspired while the Pleiades are beyond his reach.

Indeed, the speech of the Lord of mankind is worthy of being served with effort, above the head, and only the pen of the commentator, running over the paper, has fulfilled this right. My pen has long galloped along a wide course, and has often been restrained at the point of weariness and exhaustion, like a horse restrained. Now that it has reached completion, it has rightly earned the right to rest.

The completion of this commentary was on Friday afternoon, the twelfth of the month of Rajab in the year one thousand three hundred and eighty (1380 AH). The period of its composition was thirty-nine years and six months. It was a period not free of distracting occupations and other works whose branches are spreading, and disputes, with a poetic talent that at times drinks and at times is deprived, and apart from that, of scattered concerns and changing circumstances, of which the generations have never ceased to complain. And there is no ingratitude to God, for His blessings are more abundant, and the measures of His bounty upon me are neither short-weighted nor overflowing (lacking).

I ask of Him, the Exalted, for this commentary, that it may be a help and a benefit, and that it may benefit the elite and the common people, and make me among those who hope for a trade that will never perish.

Its completion was at my residence in the town of al-Marsa, east of the city of Tunis. Written by Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur.

I have brought what I hope I have been granted success in, to explain truths that are overlooked and subtleties which may have revealed aspects though not fully disclosed their essence, for this is an attainment which the human intellect cannot reach in its entirety, and whoever aspires to that has aspired while the Pleiades are beyond his reach.

Indeed, the speech of the Lord of mankind is worthy of being served with effort, above the head, and only the pen of the commentator, running over the paper, has fulfilled this right. My pen has long galloped along a wide course, and has often been restrained at the point of weariness and exhaustion, like a horse restrained. Now that it has reached completion, it has rightly earned the right to rest.

The completion of this commentary was on Friday afternoon, the twelfth of the month of Rajab in the year one thousand three hundred and eighty (1380 AH). The period of its composition was thirty-nine years and six months. It was a period not free of distracting occupations and other works whose branches are spreading, and disputes, with a poetic talent that at times drinks and at times is deprived, and apart from that, of scattered concerns and changing circumstances, of which the generations have never ceased to complain. Its completion was at my residence in the town of al-Marsa, east of the city of Tunis. Written by Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur.

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾, ﴿the King of mankind﴾, ﴿the God of mankind﴾, ﴿from the evil of the sneaking whisperer﴾, ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾, ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾.

Its opening resembles the opening of Surah al-Falaq, except that Surah al-Falaq is a seeking of refuge from the evils of created beings, such as animals and humans, while Surah al-Nas is a seeking of refuge from the evils of hidden created beings, who are the devils (al-shayatin).

The discussion regarding the command to say (this), regarding what is said, and regarding the fact that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) while the intended meaning includes his community, is the same as the discussion of its counterpart in Surah al-Falaq.

"Rabb" is made definite by its being annexed to "al-nas" (mankind), not to other beings that are nurtured, because seeking refuge from the evil that Satan casts into the hearts of people, so that they go astray and lead others astray, means that the evil sought refuge from is directed toward people. It was therefore fitting that the One sought refuge with be brought to mind by the title that He is the Lord of those who cast evil and of those to whom it is cast, so that He may turn these away and repel it from the others, as one says to the master of a slave: "O master of so-and-so, restrain your slave from me."

The attributes of God in relation to people have been arranged in a graduated order. God is their Creator; then they are not outside His judgment when He wills to dispose of their affairs; then He is further clarified by the attribute of His divinity toward them, so that it becomes clear that His lordship over them and His sovereignty over them is not like the lordship of some of them over others and the sovereignty of some of them over others.

In this ordering there is also an indication of the stages of reflection in knowing God, the Exalted. The one who reflects first declares that he has a Lord, on account of what he perceives of his own existence and the blessing of his composition. Then he delves deeper into reflection and perceives that his Lord is the true King, free of need from creation. Then he knows that He is the one deserving of worship, so He is the God of all mankind.

﴿King of mankind﴾ is an apposition (ʿatf al-bayan) to "Lord of mankind," and likewise ﴿God of mankind﴾. The repetition of the word "mankind" rather than suffice with a pronoun is because apposition requires explicitness, so that the explaining noun (in the genitive) is independent in itself, since the apposition stands in the position of a sign for the explained noun (in the accusative).

"Al-nas" is a collective noun for all of humanity or a group of them, and it is not applied, in verification, to anyone other than them.

"Al-waswas" means one who speaks with whispering, and whispering is hidden speech. Ru'ba said, describing a hunter in his hiding place:

"He whispered, calling sincerely upon the Lord of the daybreak."

So "al-waswas" is an active participle. The word "al-waswas" with a fatha on the waw is used figuratively for the thoughts that occur to a person's self, which he imagines, like speech that a person addresses to himself. ʿUrwa ibn Udhayna said:

"And when you find for it whispers of consolation, let the heart intercede with the conscience and then soothe it."

The definite article in "al-waswas" is the definite article of the genus, and the application of "al-waswas" to its literal and figurative meanings includes the devils who cast evil thoughts into people's souls, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But Satan whispered to him﴾ [Taha: 120]. It also includes every person among mankind who speaks hidden speech, namely the people of plots and conspiracies, whose purpose is to inflict harm, whether by assassinating souls, stealing wealth, or enticing [others] into error and turning away from guidance. This is because the custom of these people in discussing with one another is that it be secret, lest those they intend to harm learn of it. These are the ones who lie in wait for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for misfortunes and incite people to harm him.

"Al-khannas" means one who withdraws greatly and frequently. The intended meaning is that it has become a habit for him. "Al-khans" and "al-khunus" mean concealment. Satan is given the epithet "al-khannas" because he attaches himself to a person's intellect and resolve without any awareness on the person's part, so it is as if he has withdrawn into him. And people of deceit, scheming and stealthy approach are "khannasun," because they watch for people's moments of heedlessness and conceal themselves with various kinds of tricks so that people will not perceive them.

The definiteness of "al-khannas" is according to the pattern of the definiteness of the noun it describes. Also, because thoughts of evil occupy their owner's mind, he lowers his head and hesitates and fears their consequences, and the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) restrains him, or the restraint of religion, or shame, or fear of punishment from God or from people restrains him. Then it returns to him until he is at ease with it and becomes accustomed to it, so he resolves to do it and commits it. It is as if Satan appears to him and then disappears, then appears and disappears, until he is able to lower him into delusion with deception.

So the ultimate goal of whispering through its whisperings is to spread it into the soul of the deceived one and the one caught in its trap. "And when you find for it whispers of consolation, let the heart intercede with the conscience and then soothe it."

The definite article in "al-waswas" is the definite article of the genus, and the application of "al-waswas" to its literal and figurative meanings includes the devils who cast evil thoughts into people's souls, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But Satan whispered to him﴾ [Taha: 120]. It also includes every person among mankind who speaks hidden speech, namely the people of plots and conspiracies, whose purpose is to inflict harm, whether by assassinating souls, stealing wealth, or enticing [others] into error and turning away from guidance. This is because the custom of these people in discussing with one another is that it be secret, lest those they intend to harm learn of it. These are the ones who lie in wait for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for misfortunes and incite people to harm him.

"Al-khannas" means one who withdraws greatly and frequently. The intended meaning is that it has become a habit for him. "Al-khans" and "al-khunus" mean concealment. Satan is given the epithet "al-khannas" because he attaches himself to a person's intellect and resolve without any awareness on the person's part, so it is as if he has withdrawn into him. And people of deceit, scheming and stealthy approach are "khannasun," because they watch for people's moments of heedlessness and conceal themselves with various kinds of tricks so that people will not perceive them.

The definiteness of "al-khannas" is according to the pattern of the definiteness of the noun it describes. Also, because thoughts of evil occupy their owner's mind, he lowers his head and hesitates and fears their consequences, and the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) restrains him, or the restraint of religion, or shame, or fear of punishment from God or from people restrains him. Then it returns to him until he is at ease with it and becomes accustomed to it, so he resolves to do it and commits it. It is as if Satan appears to him and then disappears, then appears and disappears, until he is able to lower him into delusion with deception.

﴿The sneaking whisperer﴾ is described by ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾ in order to bring the image of whispering closer, so that a person may guard against it when it afflicts him, because of its concealment. This is done by clarifying that the place where whispering is cast is the breasts of people and their inner selves. Thus the breast is used to express the inner psychological sensation, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but greatness, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir: 56]. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Sin is that which stirs in the breast and wavers in the heart." So the ultimate goal of whispering through its whisperings is to spread it into the soul of the deceived one and the one caught in its trap. Thus, the whisperings of the devils are attractions linking souls toward the call of the devils. The Prophet (ﷺ) brought this closer in many reports through various kinds of comparison, among them (that they are like proboscises which Satan extends to the heart of a human being), and he likened it once to blowing, and once to ...[sic: "al-ibsas"] (the coaxing of a beast). And in the hadith: ("Satan runs in the son of Adam as blood runs, and I feared that he would cast [evil] into your hearts.")

The use of the verb "yuwaswisu" (whispers) for this satanic act is figurative, since Satan has no speech in the inner self of a person. As for its application to a person's embellishing of evil deeds for another, it is literal. The attachment of the prepositional phrase in His saying ﴿in the breasts of mankind﴾ to the verb ﴿whispers﴾ is a real attachment with respect to Satan's whispering, while with respect to people's whispering it is a rational figurative attachment, because people's whispering is a cause for its effect to occur in the breasts. So in each of the verb "yuwaswisu" and its complement there is the use of the two expressions both in the literal and the figurative sense.

The "min" in His saying ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾ is explanatory (bayaniyyah). It explains ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾ as being a genus which, considering the intention of its literal and figurative meanings, divides into two categories: one category from the jinn, which is its origin, and another category from mankind, who are only followers and allies of the first category. God combined these two categories in His saying: (﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy: devils among mankind and jinn, who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am: 112]).

The need for this clarification is the hiddenness of what results from the whispering of the human species, because nations are accustomed to their reformers warning them about Satan's whispering, and it may not occur to them that among whisperings there is one worse than the whispering of the devils, namely the whispering of the people of their own kind, which is more dangerous, and they are more deserving of seeking refuge from them, because they are closer to them and it is more hazardous for them, and because they are more capable and more able to cause harm.

It is not correct for "min" to be explanatory of "mankind," since the name "mankind" is not applied to what includes the jinn, and whoever claims that has gone far astray.

"Al-jinnah" is a collective noun for "jinniyy," with the nisba ya' referring to the species of jinn; thus a single "jinniyy" is one of the species of jinn, just as one says "insiyy" for one of mankind.

The repetition of the word "mankind" in these verses, in the first two occurrences, with respect to one meaning, is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, for the purpose of emphasizing God's lordship, His dominion, and His divinity over all of mankind, as in His saying: ﴿They twist their tongues with the Book, that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran: 78].

As for its repetition the third time with His saying ﴿in the breasts of mankind﴾, it is an explicit noun for the sake of the remoteness of the return (to the Hereafter).

As for its repetition the fourth time with His saying ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾, it is because it is an explanation of one of the two categories of "who whispers in the breasts of mankind," and that is not the same referent as the word "mankind" in the previous occurrences.

And God suffices us against the evil of the two groups, and benefits us with the goodness of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn).

The commentary on Surah al-Nas is complete, and with it the commentary on the Mighty Qur'an is complete.

Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur says: I have fulfilled what I intended, and God has realized what I hoped for. I have come with what my effort permitted of explaining the meanings of the Qur'an, the subtleties of its order and the characteristics of its eloquence, drawing from the statements of the imams what the mind could absorb, and striking a spark to illuminate thought and kindle resolve. I have brought what I hope I have been granted success in, to explain truths that are overlooked and subtleties which may have revealed aspects though not fully disclosed their essence, for this is an attainment which the human intellect cannot reach in its entirety, and whoever aspires to that has aspired while the Pleiades are beyond his reach.

Indeed, the speech of the Lord of mankind is worthy of being served with effort, above the head, and only the pen of the commentator, running over the paper, has fulfilled this right. My pen has long galloped along a wide course, and has often been restrained at the point of weariness and exhaustion, like a horse restrained. Now that it has reached completion, it has rightly earned the right to rest.

The completion of this commentary was on Friday afternoon, the twelfth of the month of Rajab in the year one thousand three hundred and eighty (1380 AH). The period of its composition was thirty-nine years and six months. It was a period not free of distracting occupations and other works whose branches are spreading, and disputes, with a poetic talent that at times drinks and at times is deprived, and apart from that, of scattered concerns and changing circumstances, of which the generations have never ceased to complain. And there is no ingratitude to God, for His blessings are more abundant, and the measures of His bounty upon me are neither short-weighted nor overflowing (lacking).

I ask of Him, the Exalted, for this commentary, that it may be a help and a benefit, and that it may benefit the elite and the common people, and make me among those who hope for a trade that will never perish.

Its completion was at my residence in the town of al-Marsa, east of the city of Tunis. Written by Muhammad al-Tahir ibn 'Ashur.
